/teensy/sensor:
# Periodic sensor snapshot from the Teensy microcontroller (topic: teensy/sensor).
# Published by: teensy node (tabletop_teensy firmware) or mock_teensy node, published periodically.
# Consumed by: TeensyInterface (tabletop_rig/interfaces/teensy.py) and Commander
#              (_teensy_sensor_callback) for safety interlock decisions.

std_msgs/Header header                        # Timestamp set on the Teensy using synchronized ROS time (rmw_uros_epoch_nanos)
bool is_safety_laser_broken                   # True when the safety laser beam is interrupted (HIGH on SAFETY_LASER_STATE_PIN); blocks robot execution
bool is_left_arm_locked                       # True when the left-hand sensor is held (debounced LOW on LEFT_ARM_LOCK_STATE_PIN, standard pin 36)
bool is_right_arm_locked                      # True when the right-hand sensor is held (debounced LOW on RIGHT_ARM_LOCK_STATE_PIN, standard pin 39)
bool is_reward_active                         # True while the juice/reward solenoid is open (REWARD_CONTROL_PIN HIGH)
bool is_button_pressed                        # Wired response input; always false in standard firmware, active-low only in a temporary --button-pin build
bool is_smartglass_revealed                   # True when the smartglass pane is transparent (SMARTGLASS_CONTROL_PIN HIGH)
uint16[5] left_tactile_glove_states           # 10-bit ADC readings (0-1023) for the 5 left-hand glove pressure sensors (pins A0-A4)
uint16[5] right_tactile_glove_states          # 10-bit ADC readings (0-1023) for the 5 right-hand glove pressure sensors (pins A5-A9)
bool sync_pulse_state                         # True while the sync pulse output (SYNC_PULSE_CONTROL_PIN) is HIGH; pulse duration ~100 ms, period ~1 s + jitter
builtin_interfaces/Time sync_pulse_last_time_on   # ROS timestamp of the most recent sync pulse rising edge
builtin_interfaces/Time sync_pulse_last_time_off  # ROS timestamp of the most recent sync pulse falling edge
builtin_interfaces/Time safety_laser_last_time_broken  # ROS timestamp of the last safety laser break event (interrupt-latched)
builtin_interfaces/Time button_last_time_pressed   # Last wired-response onset; zero in standard firmware, interrupt-latched in a temporary --button-pin build

MSG: builtin_interfaces/Time
# This message communicates ROS Time defined here:
# https://design.ros2.org/articles/clock_and_time.html

# The seconds component, valid over all int32 values.
int32 sec

# The nanoseconds component, valid in the range [0, 1e9), to be added to the seconds component. 
# e.g.
# The time -1.7 seconds is represented as {sec: -2, nanosec: 3e8}

MSG: tabletop_interfaces/Eyelink
# Single binocular gaze sample from the SR Research Eyelink eye tracker.
# Published by: eyelink node (nodes/eyelink.py, topic ~/sample) at up to 1000 Hz.
# Consumed by: EyelinkInterface (interfaces/eyelink.py) via action feedback;
#              also batched into EyelinkArray and written to rosbag.

float32 left_y              # Left eye raw pupil Y position in Eyelink camera pixel units; MISSING_DATA (-32768) when eye not tracked
float32 left_pupil          # Left eye pupil diameter in arbitrary Eyelink units (diameter mode); MISSING_DATA (-32768) when unavailable
float32 right_x             # Right eye raw pupil X position in Eyelink camera pixel units; MISSING_DATA (-32768) when eye not tracked
float32 right_y             # Right eye raw pupil Y position in Eyelink camera pixel units; MISSING_DATA (-32768) when eye not tracked
float32 right_pupil         # Right eye pupil diameter in arbitrary Eyelink units (diameter mode); MISSING_DATA (-32768) when unavailable
uint16 input                # EyeLink raw input-port value (from Sample.getInput()); current rig: status pin 12 is 127 idle, 95 asserted

/joint_states:
# This is a message that holds data to describe the state of a set of torque controlled joints.
#
# The state of each joint (revolute or prismatic) is defined by:
#  * the position of the joint (rad or m),
#  * the velocity of the joint (rad/s or m/s) and
#  * the effort that is applied in the joint (Nm or N).
#
# Each joint is uniquely identified by its name
# The header specifies the time at which the joint states were recorded. All the joint states
# in one message have to be recorded at the same time.
#
# This message consists of a multiple arrays, one for each part of the joint state.
# The goal is to make each of the fields optional. When e.g. your joints have no
# effort associated with them, you can leave the effort array empty.
#
# All arrays in this message should have the same size, or be empty.
# This is the only way to uniquely associate the joint name with the correct
# states.

std_msgs/Header header

string[] name
float64[] position
float64[] velocity
float64[] effort

/rosout:
##
## Severity level constants
## 
## These logging levels follow the Python Standard
## https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging-levels
## And are implemented in rcutils as well
## https://github.com/ros2/rcutils/blob/35f29850064e0c33a4063cbc947ebbfeada11dba/include/rcutils/logging.h#L164-L172
## This leaves space for other standard logging levels to be inserted in the middle in the future,
## as well as custom user defined levels.
## Since there are several other logging enumeration standard for different implementations,
## other logging implementations may need to provide level mappings to match their internal implementations.
##

# Debug is for pedantic information, which is useful when debugging issues.
uint8 DEBUG=10

# Info is the standard informational level and is used to report expected
# information.
uint8 INFO=20

# Warning is for information that may potentially cause issues or possibly unexpected
# behavior.
uint8 WARN=30

# Error is for information that this node cannot resolve.
uint8 ERROR=40

# Information about a impending node shutdown.
uint8 FATAL=50

##
## Fields
##

# Timestamp when this message was generated by the node.
builtin_interfaces/Time stamp

# Corresponding log level, see above definitions.
uint8 level

# The name representing the logger this message came from.
string name

# The full log message.
string msg

# The file the message came from.
string file

# The function the message came from.
string function

# The line in the file the message came from.
uint32 line

#
# meta data messages for camera images
#
std_msgs/Header header

# time stamp produced by camera, interpretation depends on camera model
uint64 camera_time

# Camera-provided monotonically increasing frame identifier. This permits
# offline detection of physical acquisition gaps independently of ROS/DDS.
uint64 camera_frame_id

# True only when header.stamp was assigned by the shared synchronized-camera
# estimator. False messages are archival fallbacks whose header uses the host
# arrival time; camera_time and camera_frame_id remain the authoritative raw
# timing identifiers for post-processing.
bool synchronized_timestamp_valid

# computed brightness, either 0...255 (valid) or -1 (invalid)
int16 brightness

# exposure time in microseconds
uint32 exposure_time

# max allowed exposure time in microseconds
uint32 max_exposure_time

# gain in db
float32 gain

# line status
int64 line_status
